title: Harmonograph
description: A sheet of warm white paper on the table of a three-pendulum harmonograph. Two pendulums swing a hairline pen arm, a ring of ink at its nib, at nearly two to three (three to four on the next sheet), a third circles the table and the paper beneath it, and the single line they draw winds inward as the swing decays, thinning where the pen runs fast and darkening where it slows. Take the pen arm, pull it out and let go, or take the paper and throw the table: the pen lifts, comes down on the swing you gave it, and the figure it finished is pulled into the sheet as a broad impression in a spot ink, vermilion, then process blue, pink and teal, halftoned at its own screen angle from the time the nib spent over each spot, darkest where its loops crowd, banded like the loops themselves, and thinning through ever smaller dots to open paper where they spread, never closing up, so paper shows through every overprint, and overprinted a hair out of register, while the pen draws on over it in a fine near-black line. Every drop adds a colour, and the sheet builds up into a layered print. The nib lifts itself once the swing has wound in, so the centre stays open, and you can hear it on the paper. Double-click to tear the sheet off the pad and start a fresh one.
intent: From the Vertigo titles (Saul Bass and John Whitney, 1958, https://artofthetitle.com/title/vertigo): machine-drawn Lissajous figures made with total precision. Here the machine is a real damped three-pendulum harmonograph, and the paper is the object.
